reader.decision: Accept the correction: the key gets the negotiated format (avif/webp/orig), not the raw Accept header. Hand it to Petra: change cache_key and reorder serve_image so negotiate runs before lookup.
reader.decision_reason: The message corrects my misstatement, giving a concrete reason (1,912 distinct Accept values in October would collapse the hit rate versus 3 format values). It also names the reorder needed in serve_image, so the ruling stands and the handoff is clear.

reconstruction.problem: img-edge caches images by path plus query only, so a WebP variant cached after Jonas Ek's Chrome request is served to Safari 13, which cannot decode WebP. Hanna Lind sees a broken image.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Safari 13 users get broken product images. Also, if the key used the raw Accept header, the hit rate would collapse (up to 1,912 entries per image). And without reordering serve_image, lookup runs before negotiate, so the key has no format and the bug stays.
reconstruction.fix: Add the negotiated format (avif, webp or orig) to the cache key: cache_key(request, image_format), with lookup and save taking image_format too. In edge/handler.py, serve_image calls negotiate first, then passes image_format to lookup and save.
reconstruction.cost: Code change in edge/cache.py and edge/handler.py (cache_key signature, lookup, save, reorder in serve_image). Up to 3 cache entries per image instead of 1. Effort and rollout cost not stated.
